title: Volubilis
summary: Volubilis, near Meknes in Morocco, was a Mauretanian capital founded in the 3rd century BCE. It grew into an important outpost of the Roman Empire and later briefly served as capital of Idris I, founder of the Idrisid dynasty. World History Encyclopedia says it was abandoned in the 11th century CE.

uncertainty.note: Start is the 3rd century BCE (-299 to -200), midpoint used; end is the 11th century CE (1000-1099), midpoint used, for abandonment per World History Encyclopedia.

as_recorded.value: developed from the 3rd century BCE onwards
It was abandoned 1,400 years later, in the 11th century CE
